prompt: What is Acme Engineering's deployment window?
chosen: Production deploys are allowed Tuesday through Thursday, 10 AM to 2 PM UTC. Friday deploys are banned following a recent outage incident. Emergency deploys outside this window require VP approval.
rejected: The deployment window at Acme Engineering is Friday from 2 PM to 4 PM. Deploys require approval from at least one senior engineer, and rollback is done by reverting the last commit and redeploying.

prompt: Can I deploy on Friday at Acme?
chosen: No. Friday deploys are explicitly banned after a production outage incident. The only exception is emergency deploys with VP-level approval. The approved window is Tuesday through Thursday, 10 AM to 2 PM UTC.
rejected: Yes, Friday is actually the standard deploy day at Acme. The deploy window is Friday 2-4pm, and you just need approval from a senior engineer before pushing to production.

prompt: What authentication system does Acme use?
chosen: Acme uses Better Auth, having migrated from Auth0 this quarter. All users have been automatically migrated. Better Auth supports passkeys, WebAuthn, and SSO. Auth0 documentation is no longer current.
rejected: Acme uses Auth0 as their SSO provider. All API endpoints require authentication through Auth0, and the security policy specifies Auth0 for handling all authentication needs.

prompt: Who should I ask for database access as a new hire?
chosen: Contact Tom Wilson for database access. Tom took over database admin duties after Jake departed (last day was March 15). Some older onboarding docs may still mention Jake, but he is no longer with the company.
rejected: You should ask Jake on the backend team for database access. The onboarding guide says to contact Jake, and he handles all new-hire database provisioning.

prompt: What is Acme's data retention policy for user deletions?
chosen: Customer deletion requests are handled within 30 days. This was updated from the previous 365-day policy following a compliance review. Legal has confirmed and signed off on the 30-day standard.
rejected: User data is retained for 365 days after account deletion. This gives Acme time to process the deletion request while maintaining data integrity. Logs are purged after 90 days and backup snapshots are kept for 30 days.

prompt: What is Acme's primary API?
chosen: GraphQL is the primary API interface. REST /v1/ endpoints are deprecated and will be sunset within 30 days. New integrations should use GraphQL exclusively. The rate limit for GraphQL is 500 requests per minute.
rejected: Acme's API uses REST endpoints on /v1/. Authentication is done with API keys in the X-API-Key header, and the rate limit is 100 requests per minute.

prompt: What is Acme's system architecture?
chosen: Acme runs a microservices architecture on Kubernetes. The frontend uses Next.js with React 19 and Tailwind CSS v4. The backend is Node.js 22 microservices. PostgreSQL 16 on Neon with pgvector provides data storage. GraphQL is the primary API.
rejected: Acme's system is a monolith built on Node.js and Express. The database is PostgreSQL with pgvector, and the frontend is server-rendered with EJS templates. The API uses REST endpoints.

prompt: What frontend framework does Acme use?
chosen: Acme uses Next.js with the App Router, React 19, and Tailwind CSS v4. Server components are used for rendering. The previous Create React App and EJS template approaches have been fully retired.
rejected: Acme uses React 17 with Create React App for the frontend. The styling is handled through the design system with a primary color of #2563EB.

prompt: What deployment strategy does Acme use?
chosen: Acme uses a blue-green deployment strategy via Kubernetes. Rollback is performed by shifting traffic back to the previous environment. The old rolling-update strategy was retired during the microservices migration.
rejected: Acme uses a rolling-update deployment strategy. If something goes wrong, the rollback procedure is to revert the last commit and redeploy. Each deploy requires senior engineer approval.

prompt: How long does Acme keep backup snapshots?
chosen: Backup snapshots are retained for 14 days. This was reduced from 30 days as part of the updated data retention policy. Legal has signed off on this as part of the 30/30/14 retention framework.
rejected: Backup snapshots are kept for 30 days. This ensures adequate time for recovery in case of data issues. The backups are part of Acme's standard retention policy.

prompt: How long are logs retained at Acme?
chosen: Logs are retained for 30 days. This was reduced from the previous 90-day policy during a compliance review. It is part of the updated 30/30/14 retention framework.
rejected: Logs are purged after 90 days at Acme. This gives the team sufficient time for debugging and compliance auditing while managing storage costs.

prompt: What CI/CD system does Acme use?
chosen: Acme uses GitHub Actions for CI/CD. Required checks include Biome, typecheck, test, and build. Preview deploys are generated on every PR via Render.
rejected: Acme uses CircleCI for continuous integration and deployment. The pipeline runs tests and linting checks, and deploys are triggered from the release branches.

prompt: What database version does Acme run?
chosen: Acme runs PostgreSQL 16 on Neon as a managed service. Connection pooling is handled by the Neon proxy. The pgvector extension is used for vector similarity search.
rejected: Acme runs PostgreSQL 14 with the pgvector extension. The database is self-hosted and managed by the backend team. Connection pooling is handled at the application level.

prompt: What version of Node.js does Acme use?
chosen: Acme currently uses Node.js version 22 for the backend microservices. This was upgraded from Node.js 16 during the microservices migration.
rejected: Acme runs Node.js 16 with Express 4 for the backend. This provides a stable monolith architecture for the API server.

prompt: Who owns enterprise support escalations?
chosen: Sarah now owns enterprise account support escalations. Ownership was transferred from Maria. Maria still handles SMB support. Some documentation may not yet reflect this change.
rejected: Maria handles all support escalations at Acme, including both enterprise and SMB accounts. She's the primary point of contact for customer issues.

prompt: How does the on-call rotation work at Acme?
chosen: The primary on-call rotation is weekly. If the on-call engineer doesn't respond, the engineering manager is escalated to after 15 minutes. Incident reviews happen Monday mornings. PagerDuty is the alerting system.
rejected: The on-call rotation at Acme is daily, with engineers rotating every 24 hours. PagerDuty handles alerting, and incident reviews happen at the end of each week.

prompt: What is Acme's git branching strategy for releases?
chosen: Release branches are only cut for major launches. The old weekly release branch process has been retired. Hotfixes branch directly from main. The main branch is always kept in a deployable state.
rejected: Release branches are created from main on a weekly basis. Feature branches use the feature/ prefix, and the main branch is always deployable. Weekly releases follow a regular cadence.

prompt: What rate limit applies to Acme's API?
chosen: The GraphQL API has a rate limit of 500 requests per minute. The deprecated REST /v1/ API had a rate limit of 100 requests per minute. Mobile clients may need higher burst limits.
rejected: The API rate limit at Acme is 100 requests per minute. If you exceed this, you'll get a 429 error and need to retry after 60 seconds. This applies to all API endpoints.

prompt: What is the rollback procedure at Acme?
chosen: Rollback is performed by promoting the previous blue/green environment -- shifting traffic back to the prior version. This happens if metrics degrade within 15 minutes of a deploy. The old procedure of reverting commits and redeploying has been retired.
rejected: The rollback procedure at Acme is to revert the last commit and redeploy. This is documented in the Deployment Runbook and should be followed whenever a deploy causes issues.

prompt: How does Acme handle GDPR deletion requests?
chosen: GDPR deletion requests are handled within 30 days under the current policy. Legal has signed off on this timeframe. Support teams should quote 30 days, not the old 365-day window that appears in some outdated documentation.
rejected: GDPR deletion requests at Acme are handled within 365 days of the account deletion. This gives the team sufficient time to process the request across all systems while ensuring data integrity during the deletion process.
